interest: Shows 1930s US tracking of suspected Japanese espionage near Panama Canal via fishing, oil, and mineral ventures in Latin America.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.20210, File 410) consists of docket lists of papers compiled between 1934 and 1939 detailing Japanese military activities, espionage, intelligence gathering, and infiltration throughout Latin America and the vicinity of the Panama Canal Zone, along with a 1932 jacket case docket sheet regarding alleged subversive activities by Motoichi Kurikawa. The docket records inter-agency discussions and intelligence sharing among the State Department, the War Department's Military Intelligence Division (M.I.D.), the Navy Department (11th and 15th Naval Districts), and the Governor of the Panama Canal Zone, focusing on monitoring Japanese activities in Central America, Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, Peru, Mexico, and Uruguay. Key matters tracked include Japanese foreign office espionage funding under a purported 'Cultural Office', surveillance of Japanese fishing vessels and engineers conducting coastal and mineral surveys, oil exploration contracts, press reporting, and diplomatic cooperation with Latin American governments to curb Japanese encroachment, with nearly all substantive documents cross-referenced to related regional and economic decimal files.

subfiles.about: State Department docket list summarizing incoming and outgoing correspondence, memoranda, and intelligence reports regarding Japanese military, espionage, and economic activities in Latin America between 1934 and 1939.
subfiles.summary: Four-page docket (Form 10-45) listing 25 items, 1934-39, on suspected Japanese espionage threatening the Panama Canal Zone, tracking State-War-Navy coordination, fishing and mineral surveys as intelligence fronts, and Latin American government responses; most entries cross-reference other decimal files.
